title: River Biofilms Sampling for DNA Analysis and Microscopic Counts
author: Frederic Rimet

steps.title: Prepare Equipment and Cleaning
steps.instruction: Ensure all equipment is clean to avoid contamination.

substeps.instruction: Use new nylon brushes (e.g., toothbrushes).
Clean the lab tray with 10% H2O2, rinse with DNA-free water, and dry.
Wear gloves throughout the sampling process and change them between different sampling stations.

steps.title: Select Sampling Season and Station
steps.instruction: Choose the sampling period and location based on hydrological conditions and substrate availability.

substeps.instruction: Sample during the natural low-water period (e.g., summer in Europe) under clear water conditions.
If low-intensity hydrological events occurred, wait a few days before sampling.
If intense hydrological events occurred (lasting floods or support reworking), wait 3-4 weeks before sampling.
Select stations on natural or artificialized watercourses, excluding naturally salted stretches (e.g., estuaries).
Ensure substrates have been submerged for several weeks; avoid sampling too close to the surface.
If the station is not predefined, sample a stretch of minimum 20m/40m or 4-5 times the width of the running water body.

steps.title: Collect Biofilm from Stones
steps.instruction: Collect biofilm from natural hard substrates if available.

substeps.instruction: Select at least 5 stones (or more depending on size/biofilm amount) for a total brushed surface of at least 100 cm².
Collect stones at 20-50 cm depth from the minimal annual water level within a 100 m² area (at least 2 m wide).
Let the stones drain for a few minutes.
Fill the bottom of the tray with 50 ml of absolute ethanol.
Brush the stones in the tray to collect biological material.

steps.title: Process Samples from Stones
steps.instruction: Sub-sample the biofilm/water mixture from the tray for DNA and microscopy analysis.

substeps.instruction: For DNA samples: Transfer the mixture into a 50 mL tube up to 10 ml, add ~40 mL of absolute ethanol to reach 50 ml, shake to homogenize, and label.
For microscopy samples: Transfer a second 10 mL sub-sample into a tube and add either 70% Ethanol or 2% Formaldehyde as the preservative.
For live inspection (soft algae): Keep a third sub-sample without fixation.

steps.title: Collect Biofilm from Alternative Substrates
steps.instruction: If stones are unavailable, use artificial substrates or macrophytes.

substeps.instruction: For artificial hard substrates (e.g., riprap, concrete banks): Use a hoe equipped with a net to scrap a minimal surface of 100 cm³ at 20-40 cm depth.
For macrophytes: At 20-40 cm depth, squeeze submerged filaments (e.g., Elodea, Potamogeton) or scrap the stem (e.g., Typha), ensuring at least 20 cm of stem is scrapped.
Note: If macrophytes are used, indicate this on the sample; only diatom analyses will be performed.

steps.title: Prepare Blank Samples
steps.instruction: Create a blank sample approximately every 10 stations for DNA analysis.

substeps.instruction: Fill the bottom of a clean tray with 50 ml of DNA-free water.
Fill a 50 mL sterile Falcon tube up to 10 ml with the water from the tray.
Complete the tube with ~40 mL of absolute ethanol to reach 50 ml.
Shake to homogenize and label.

steps.title: Store and Label Samples
steps.instruction: Label and store all samples according to their intended analysis.

substeps.instruction: Label samples with: 'Biofilm', 'River Name', 'Station', and 'Date'.
Store DNA samples and blanks at ~ +4°C in the dark for maximum 1 month, or freeze at -20 or -80°C for maximum 3 months.
Store microscopy samples (fixed or live) at ~ +4°C in the dark.
Complete field sheets with mesological data and provide photographic documentation of the sampling area if possible.
